business_scope.primary_industry_name: Specialty Fresh Bakery Master Franchise and Central Kitchen Ops

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Codified: Code civil and Code de commerce; Romanist doctrine with an autonomous system of administrative courts)

WTO framework (both states WTO members; TRIMS and GATS schedules apply to franchise and central-kitchen service operations)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary AML/CFT statutes: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-57 and R. 561-1 to R. 561-67, transposing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Law No. 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II), Articles 139-142 establishing the register of beneficial owners; Decree No. 2021-263 of 9 March 2021 and Arrêté of 28 April 2021 governing the UBO register filings; Regulation (EU) 2015/847 (transfer of funds); Council Regulations (EU) No. 269/2014 and No. 833/2014 directly applicable for asset freezing and sectoral sanctions; Law No. 2019-486 of 22 May 2019 (PACTE) and Law No. 2020-1525 of 7 December 2020 transferring the corporate and UBO registries to the Registre National des Entreprises opérational since 1 January 2023 under INPI administration.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal — The Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) at the RNE/INPI is not freely accessible to the public following the Conseil d'État ruling of 18 October 2023 implementing CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20). Access is restricted to: (i) competent authorities (Tracfin, tax, customs, judicial authorities, préfectures); (ii) AMF/ACPR-supervised financial institutions and other AML/CFT obliged entities performing customer due diligence; and (iii) persons demonstrating a legitimate interest (journalists, sectoral NGOs).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the shareholder's national passport (identity and signature pages)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC notary public (公证处) followed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China (apostille section)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille — PRC notarization then PRC MFA apostille; no French consular legalization required (France accepts Chinese apostilles with effect from 1 March 2007 under the 1961 Hague Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (无犯罪记录证明) for each proposed manager, président and officer of the SAS
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC Public Security Bureau (公安局/派出所), notarized and subsequently apostilled by the PRC MFA
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (notarization + PRC MFA apostille; certified French translation required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current proof of residential address (bank statement or utility bill dated within three months before filing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC financial institution or utility provider, notarized and apostilled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (notarization + PRC MFA apostille; certified French translation required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate due diligence pack for any corporate shareholder (certificate of incorporation, register of shareholders showing the UBO chain to natural persons, statutory audit opinion, board resolution authorizing the French investment)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) extracts, corporate registers and sealed board resolutions, notarized and apostilled
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (notarization + PRC MFA apostille; certified French translation required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Business plan and pro-forma financial projections for the bakery chain (required by the French bank's compliance department and for the capital deposit attestation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant's local counsel or licensed financial advisor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; must be submitted in French or with a certified French translation for bank CDD purposes

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening per Article L. 561-10 of the Monetary and Financial Code: all beneficial owners, officers, managers and authorized signatories of the SAS must be screened for PEP status (domestic and foreign, including family members and close associates per FATF R.18) before bank onboarding. Consecutive automated screening is required against: (i) the EU consolidated financial sanctions database (EEAS); (ii) the UN Security Council consolidated list; (iii) the US OFAC SDN list (mandatory because the master royalty wire rails are USD-cleared); and (iv) the French Treasury asset-freezing file at gels-avoir.dgtresor.gouv.fr. Secondary-source verification and adverse-media checks apply to Chinese natural-person UBOs residing outside the EU under the ACPR guidelines on customer due diligence. Suspicion reporting to Tracfin is mandatory irrespective of amount (Article L. 561-15 of the Monetary and Financial Code) and is legally privileged and non-disclosable to the client.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) administered by INPI — https://registre-national-entreprises.fr; electronic filing and name-filing channel: https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); public pre-clearance search of taken names and trademarks: https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name (dénomination sociale) of an SAS must be stated in the articles of association in French or in any language transcribed in Latin (roman) script. Chinese-script brand elements are permitted only as a secondary or trademark element, never as the official registered name; a pinyin or romanized transliteration is mandatory for the RNE field. All statutory filings, the articles, and the UBO declaration must be drafted or translated by a sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) into French. The name must be lawful, not misleading (Article L. 711-3 of the Intellectual Property Code), and must not infringe earlier trademark, company-name or domain rights (Article L. 711-4). Third-party names already present in the RNE and in the INPI trademark database must be avoided; a pre-filing clearance against the RNE, data.inpi.fr and EUIPO TMview is recommended.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Avocat / Notaire / Expert-Comptable / Commissaire aux Comptes
État / République / Président de la République / Ministère / Préfecture / Mairie
France (generally prohibited where likely to mislead the public about official or national endorsement; requires case-by-case clearance)
Croix-Rouge / ONU / UNESCO / Union Européenne / OTAN / FMI / Banque Mondiale (protected emblems and international organization names)
Bio / Biologique / Halal / Fermier (regulated certification terms requiring unrelated prior certification authority approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory positive name-reservation registry akin to common-law jurisdictions; priority attaches upon the single filing through the Guichet Unique and publication of the formation notice. The 30-day window refers to the enforceable validity of the pre-filing clearance certificate and the preliminary trademark search. Procedure upon name rejection: (1) The RNE/Guichet Unique notifies the rejection with the precise legal ground (dénomination inexistante, misleading, infringement of prior rights, or use of a sensitive token). (2) The applicant corrects and re-submits the complete electronic file via formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr without additional INPI fees unless a new legal-announcement publication is needed. (3) Where the rejection stems from a ministerial prerequisite for a sensitive token, the applicant may file a written request for prior authorization with the relevant ministry; a refusal is challengeable before the administrative courts within two months of notification. (4) For procedural refusals attributed to INPI/RNE, a written appeal may be lodged with the INPI Director-General within two months under Articles R. 411-5 to R. 411-14 of the Intellectual Property Code by extension of the trademark-office analogy, followed by an appeal to the Paris Administrative Court. (5) Third-party name conflicts are resolved in summary proceedings (référé) before the President of the Commercial Court under Article 873 of the Code of Civil Procedure, where the earlier right holder may obtain an order compelling the change of the offending name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. The SAS registered seat may be domiciled at the principal place of management, at leased third-party premises, or at a licensed domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) under Articles L. 123-11 and R. 123-200 et seq. of the French Commercial Code. A virtual office is acceptable for the administrative seat of this bakery chain during the pre-opening phase, but the standard domiciliation contract is limited to two-year renewable tranches with a maximum of four years. Critically, the central kitchen and each retail POS outlet must have their own physical operational address: the DDPP will not accept a virtual address for the food-establishment declaration or the sanitary authorization, and French banks commonly require a physical operating location before activating royalty collection and POS settlement services.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Central kitchen: 100% probability of a mandatory pre-opening sanitary visit and prior authorization by the DDPP (Direction Départementale de la Protection des Populations) under Regulation (EC) No. 852/2004; thereafter approximately 80% probability of at least one unannounced DDPP hygiene inspection within the first 12 months of operation (bakery classed as moderate-risk, priority category 2). Retail POS stores: 35-45% probability per site per year of an unannounced hygiene or consumer-affairs inspection. Virtual registered office: less than 5% probability of physical inspection by the registry; however, the domiciliation company itself is required to maintain verifiable premises and an identified manager.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External French law firm (avocat inscrit au barreau) with corporate and AML practice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing French market benchmark: flat fee for a standard SAS incorporation file of USD 2,500-3,200 (EUR 2,300-2,900) excluding court and translation disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and prior-rights search against the RNE registry, INPI trademark database and EUIPO TMview (bakery/franchise class 30 and class 43)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for one international class screening EUR 120-180; statutory database consultation is free of charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PRC notarization and apostille bundle (passport, clean criminal record, proof of address, corporate UBO pack for foreign shareholders)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Chinese notary office (公证处) and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China (consular department)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: PRC statutory fee schedule: notarization RMB 200-350 per document plus apostille seal RMB 50-100 per document; aggregate estimate for four to six documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French sworn translator (traducteur assermenté auprès de la cour d'appel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-page tariff of EUR 55-85 per page; estimated four to six pages plus certification certificates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark EUR 90-120 per month for an SAS administrative seat with mail forwarding and lease-term clause

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.227-1 to L.227-20, R.123-1 to R.123-30, and R.227-1 to R.227-2; French Civil Code Articles 1832 and 1835; Monetary and Financial Code Articles L.561-46 and related provisions on beneficial-owner disclosure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), with registration in the Registre national des entreprises (RNE) and the local Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS) maintained by the competent commercial court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Online declaration of creation of a company submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the executed SAS articles of association, beneficial-owner declaration, registered-office evidence, and legal-notice publication certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital applies to an SAS. The articles determine the capital and subscription terms. At least 50% of cash contributions must be paid upon incorporation; the balance may be paid within five years of registration. Contributions in kind must be fully contributed at incorporation. A deposit certificate from a bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations is required for cash capital before registration. There is no mandatory escrow account after registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The President and shareholders resolve that the Company accept the subscriptions for all shares comprising its issued share capital, with cash contributions deposited in accordance with the subscription schedule and applicable law. The registered office is established at [full French address], effective immediately. [Name] is appointed President for an indefinite term, with authority to represent the Company within the limits of the law and the articles. [Name], if applicable, is appointed Directeur Général. The officers are authorised to complete all bank, registry, tax, beneficial-owner, employment, and licensing formalities required for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve and evidence the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises and, where applicable, the competent commercial court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a lawful registered-office address in France. Obtain a lease, domiciliation agreement, title document, or President's home-address evidence permitted by law. If a domiciliation company is used, verify that it holds the required professional domiciliation authorization. Retain the document for electronic filing.
required_dossiers: Registered-office lease, domiciliation agreement, or ownership evidence
Domiciliation provider authorization details, if applicable
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Replace defective address evidence, provide a current utility or occupancy document, and resubmit through the Guichet unique. If the registry rejects the address, request written grounds and submit corrected evidence or an amended registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute SAS constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private execution by shareholders, followed by filing through the Guichet unique
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French-language articles covering corporate name, form, purpose, capital, share rights, transfers, governance, President powers, decisions of shareholders, financial year, and dissolution. Execute the articles electronically or manually. Notarization is not generally required for cash contributions; a notarial deed is required where real property is contributed. Obtain certified translations for foreign-language supporting documents where requested.
required_dossiers: Translation and legalization or apostille documents for foreign corporate shareholders, if required
Special valuation report for contributions in kind, unless a lawful statutory waiver applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent corporate names, capital figures, powers, signatures, or shareholder data. Re-execute the affected pages and upload a consolidated corrected version.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized journal for legal notices in the registered-office department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a legal notice of incorporation to an authorized journal. Ensure that the notice states the corporate name, form, capital, registered office, purpose, term, President, transfer restrictions, and relevant registration information. Pay the applicable department-based fixed tariff and obtain the publication certificate.
required_dossiers: Final executed articles or approved notice data
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Publish a corrective notice if material information is inaccurate, obtain an updated certificate, and upload both notices where the registry requests evidence of correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the capital deposit account and obtain the certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, notary, or Caisse des dépôts et consignations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the executed articles, subscription list, identity documents, source-of-funds information, and beneficial-owner information to the depositary. Deposit at least 50% of cash subscriptions. Obtain the certificate of deposit and attach it to the incorporation filing. After registration, provide the Kbis extract to release the funds into the Company's operating account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank KYC or source-of-funds queries, replace incomplete identification documents, and obtain a corrected deposit certificate before filing or resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: INPI Guichet unique for formalities, RNE, and competent RCS registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic creation declaration, articles, legal-notice certificate, capital-deposit certificate, registered-office evidence, officer declarations, and beneficial-owner declaration. Pay the applicable registration and beneficial-owner charges. Monitor the filing dashboard and preserve the electronic acknowledgment, SIREN, SIRET, and Kbis extract when issued.
required_dossiers: President and officer declarations of non-conviction and parentage
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer registry queries within the stated deadline, upload missing or corrected documents, pay any supplementary charge, and request reconsideration or judicial review of a formal refusal through the competent commercial court procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, social, banking, and governance activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service des impôts des entreprises, URSSAF, commercial bank, and Company officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate the operating bank account, confirm corporate-tax and VAT positions with the Service des impôts des entreprises, register as an employer before hiring, maintain the statutory register of shareholder decisions, and implement accounting, invoicing, payroll, and beneficial-owner update controls. Obtain an EU VAT number where applicable.
required_dossiers: Articles and first board or shareholder resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct tax or social-registration data with the relevant authority, submit missing declarations, and preserve written confirmation of the effective registration date.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction départementale de la protection des populations (DDPP) for food establishment controls and the Préfecture, generally through the Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), for environmental and ICPE matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food-establishment declaration under French Rural and Maritime Fishing Code Article R.233-4; where the central kitchen supplies products of animal origin to other establishments, sanitary approval (agrément sanitaire) under Article L.233-2 and applicable implementing provisions. Local premises may also require an établissement recevant du public (ERP) opening authorization.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), under the authority of the competent Préfecture and the French Ministry for Ecological Transition
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Case-by-case screening or exemption, depending on project size, land-use characteristics, emissions, energy equipment, and applicable ICPE thresholds under French Environmental Code Articles L.122-1 and R.122-2. A full EIA is not automatically required for an ordinary bakery or pastry kitchen.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Connect wastewater only under the local sewer authority's conditions and obtain a discharge agreement where required. Control grease, flour solids, cleaning chemicals, and food effluent before discharge. Comply with applicable ICPE and local limits for combustion emissions, noise, odors, and VOCs; there is no single bakery-wide VOC threshold. Segregate bio-waste, used cooking oil, packaging, and hazardous cleaning waste, use authorized contractors, and retain waste-transfer and traceability records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain ERP fire-safety and accessibility approval from the competent municipality and Préfecture process before public opening where required. Maintain fire detection, extinguishers, emergency exits, electrical and gas safety, ventilation, and evacuation systems. Obtain landlord or municipal authorization for structural loads and heavy ovens, verify extraction and chimney compliance, complete required workplace risk assessment documentation, and implement occupational controls for heat, burns, flour dust, allergens, machinery, manual handling, and chemical exposure.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) - French national tax authority; official portal: impots.gouv.fr; business registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (Guichet Unique); e-invoicing/fiscal data portal: Chorus Pro (Portail Public de Facturation).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned French SAS: (1) The non-resident shareholder appoints a qualified representative, prepares the articles of association, and files incorporation via the Guichet Unique. (2) Incorporation automatically generates SIREN/SIRET registration through INPI. (3) The SAS must open a French registered office and obtain its numéro d'identification TVA intracommunautaire (FR + 11-digit key) from the competent DGFiP business tax office once taxable French supplies commence. (4) A foreign entity without a French permanent establishment that only makes B2B supplies into France generally does not need French VAT registration where the customer self-assesses under reverse charge; distance sales to French consumers may be reported under the EU OSS/non-union scheme. (5) A French SAS with non-resident shareholders must also file the annual tax return for legal entities and maintain an economic substance file sufficient to avoid constructive permanent establishment exposure under Article 209 I CGI.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a US-style check-the-box election. An SAS is automatically subject to entity-level corporate income tax (IS) on its worldwide profits to the extent the business is managed and controlled in France. Available statutory elections relevant to the SAS structure: (i) election to form a tax-integrated group / fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI where the parent holds at least 95% control; (ii) election for joint filing of VAT via the group VAT registration regime for closely-linked persons (assujetti unique) if conditions are met; (iii) no election is available to treat an SAS as a pass-through entity; and (iv) French hybrid mismatch rules operate automatically and non-electronically, with no proactive election available to alter the default mismatch treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée; French Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic economic turnover threshold triggers VAT registration in France. Any taxable person carrying out taxable supplies in France, including a foreign supplier, must register for French VAT unless the transaction benefits from reverse charge or the non-union OSS scheme for distance sales. The EUR 10,000 intra-EU distance-selling threshold concerns only cross-border intra-Community distance sales and does not remove French physical/natural place-of-supply nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory B2B e-invoicing under the French reform: from 1 September 2026, all taxable persons established in France must be able to receive e-invoices; large and mid-sized enterprises must issue structured e-invoices from 1 September 2026; small enterprises follow from 1 September 2027. E-invoices must be transmitted through a certified Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP) or the Public Invoicing Portal (Chorus Pro/PPF) using structured formats (Factur-X, UBL, CII). Real-time e-reporting (données de transaction) is required for cross-border B2B/B2C flows and payment-related data. France does not currently use pre-approval fiscal stamping; instead, DGFiP performs centralised real-time data clearance and audit analytics through the PPF/PDP network.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of bakery, Chinese pastry, and food goods from metropolitan France to a destination outside the EU qualify for the 0% export VAT rate (exonération avec droit à déduction) under Article 262-I-1 CGI if: (i) the goods physically leave French territory for the non-EU destination; (ii) the transfer of ownership to the non-EU buyer occurs; (iii) the goods are exported under a valid customs export declaration; and (iv) export is completed within the statutory timeframe. Ancillary franchise royalty services, branding fees, and services directly connected with exported goods may also be zero-rated where the place of supply is effectively outside the EU or the services are directly linked to the export transaction under the VAT place-of-supply rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation EXA / DAU) with MRN number and customs exit validation
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or CMR transport document proving physical removal from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer proof evidencing settlement by the non-EU buyer
Commercial invoice describing the goods, quantity, unit price, incoterms, and destination
Packing list / weight certificate for customs and DGFiP verification
Phytosanitary certificate, veterinary/health certificate, or other agrifood export certificate where required
Buyer due diligence / KYC file confirming the non-EU status of the foreign customer
Certificate of origin or supporting non-preferential/preferential origin documents where applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP subjects export zero-rating files to stringent documentary audit. If the 0% rate is applied without timely and complete proof of physical export, or if goods are diverted into the French/EU domestic market, the VAT is retroactively clawed back together with disallowed input VAT. Late-payment interest (intérêt de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month, and graduated penalties apply: 40% for bad-faith declarations, 80% for intentional fraud or abusive arrangement, and criminal tax/fraud prosecution exposure for submission of false documents. Customs authorities may additionally apply seizure, confiscation, and customs fines where export declarations are irregular. Related-party export transactions, repeated credit-note adjustments, high-value pastry deliveries to franchisees outside the EU, and cash POS transactions receive heightened audit scrutiny.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France maintains full convertibility for both current and capital accounts under EU and IMF standards. Profit remittances to shareholders are permitted without restriction provided supporting documentation is maintained for tax and regulatory purposes. Capital account transactions such as equity injections require prior declaration to the Banque de France via specific reporting channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French exporters must surrender foreign exchange proceeds denominated in foreign currency to a French bank account within 90 days of receipt for most goods transactions. This rule applies to bakery-related exports of ingredients or finished products. Services and intangible exports generally do not trigger surrender obligations. All surrender transactions require matching commercial invoices, packing lists, and customs declarations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore electronic money institutions face strict legal constraints in France under the Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the French Monetary and Financial Code. Cross-border digital payment solutions require local payment institution licensing or regulated partnerships, severely limiting full offshore EMI functionality for French entities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory for initial corporate account opening and KYC interviews involving directors and authorized signatories. Remote digital onboarding is permitted only for subsequent low-value transactions or accounts using eIDAS-compliant digital identity verification tools.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate shareholder registry extract, ultimate beneficial owner declaration form, and source of wealth documentation
Sanctions screening certificate, PEP declaration, and enhanced due diligence report
Reconciliation statements, commercial invoices, and proof of economic purpose

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 wires referencing the recipient's IBAN. Purpose codes include 'CAPI' for capital contributions and 'EQTY' for equity injections. All wires require matching beneficiary details, purpose code, and supporting documentation for KYC and tax compliance verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements utilize SWIFT MT103 for direct bank transfers, Commercial Letters of Credit (LCs) under UCP 600 rules, and correspondent banking channels. For bakery chain operations involving ingredient imports or product exports, standard trade finance instruments apply with proper invoice and packing list verification.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward FX contracts for hedging currency exposure
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for Asian currency pairs
Currency swaps for multi-currency liquidity optimization

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual approval of accounts and allocation of profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end, unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Potential judicial injunction, daily penalty payment, director liability, and enforcement measures; persistent non-compliance may support administrative removal from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts and related documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique and competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the accounts, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may lead to an injunction and daily penalty payment; statutory fines may reach approximately EUR 1,500, or EUR 3,000 for repeat violations, with possible administrative register removal after prolonged non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, Form 2065 and financial schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, generally by the second business day after 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest generally applies at 0.20% per month, plus a surcharge generally ranging from 10% to 80% depending on the circumstances and tax procedure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return and settlement, if subject to the normal VAT regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual CA12 filing is generally due within three months after the financial year-end; monthly or quarterly CA3 filings apply where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest and tax surcharges may apply; repeated failures may trigger audit, collection enforcement, or suspension of VAT compliance privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique and competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No routine annual filing; file an amendment generally within 30 days after a change in beneficial ownership or control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to declare or maintain accurate beneficial ownership information may result in injunctions, criminal penalties, director liability, and restrictions affecting the entity's registration or operations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of three thresholds: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory audit rules may apply to qualifying groups, entities controlled by another entity, or regulated activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) rules. IFRS may apply to qualifying consolidated accounts or where legally permitted and elected.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual beneficial ownership confirmation. The UBO register must be updated promptly after any change in ownership, voting rights, control, or personal particulars, generally within 30 days. Share transfers must be recorded in the company's share-transfer records and reflected in the beneficial ownership filing when they alter control or ownership information.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members or shareholder account records
Register of share transfers and individual shareholder accounts
Register of Directors and corporate officers
Minutes book of shareholder decisions and corporate decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 per year for a commercial registered-office or domiciliation service; France does not generally require a separate registered-agent fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,200-8,700 per year for a small SAS requiring a statutory auditor; higher fees apply to groups, regulated activities, or complex operations.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 30% of qualifying expenses); Patent box regime for qualifying IP income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Déclaration de résultat (Formulaire 1200) via impots.gouv.fr electronic filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 15 March following the fiscal year-end (e.g., 15 March for FY ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report group consolidated revenue if required; foreign parent may need to provide consolidation worksheets
Calculated after deducting all allowable expenses including transfer prices
Apply 25% rate to taxable base; claim any applicable credits or incentives

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty €750 minimum to €75,000 maximum plus 0.5% of turnover per month of delay; criminal sanctions for fraudulent filing

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions to corporate shareholders (participation exemption); 12.8% for individual recipients
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and beneficial ownership declaration to French tax authorities for DTA relief; file TRC application via impots.gouv.fr
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25%, reduced to 0-15% under most DTAs; Interest: statutory 25%, reduced to 0% under bilateral treaties with China and many jurisdictions

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million consolidated group revenue for mandatory local file and master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has transposed EU Economic Substance Directive; applies to pure tax haven structures but not to genuine operating entities like bakery chain with local employees and operations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-filing or late filing of tax returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to submit annual corporate tax return or late submission beyond grace period
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines ranging from €750 to €75,000 plus daily surcharges of 0.5% of turnover; possible criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for tax debts; potential disqualification, fines, and imprisonment for willful non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's length transfer prices without contemporaneous documentation or economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments increasing taxable profits by 500% of understated amount; penalties up to 5% of turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil and criminal liability including restitution orders and possible jail sentences for fraudulent conduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Underpayment of taxes or profit shifting evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misrepresentation of income, expenses, or related party transactions to reduce French tax base
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax evasion penalties including fines up to 500% of evaded tax and imprisonment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, asset seizure, and potential travel bans for directors involved in evasion
